title: Module 1 – Personal Website
overview: Built a personal Flask website with Home, Contact, and Projects pages using Jinja2 templates and a shared navigation layout.
learned: I learned how Flask's template inheritance and Blueprint routing work together to build a multi-page site cleanly.

title: Module 2 – GradCafe Web Scraper
overview: Built a Selenium and BeautifulSoup scraper to collect graduate admissions results from TheGradCafe, then cleaned and standardized the data.
learned: I learned how to reverse-engineer a real website's structure and handle messy, inconsistent scraped data through a proper cleaning pipeline.

title: Module 3 – PostgreSQL & Flask Dashboard
overview: Loaded scraped admissions data into PostgreSQL and built a Flask dashboard answering analytical questions with SQL queries.
learned: I learned how to write correct, precise SQL queries and how easy it is for subtle filtering bugs to quietly skew results.

title: Module 4 – Testing & Application Structure
overview: Refactored the Flask app into a testable factory pattern and built a pytest suite covering routes, database inserts, and busy-state handling.
learned: I learned how to design code with real injectable seams so it can be tested meaningfully, not just superficially.

title: Module 5 – Security & CI/CD
overview: Hardened the application with environment-based credentials, packaging via setup.py, and a GitHub Actions pipeline running pylint, tests, and security scans.
learned: I learned that a passing lint score can hide real issues if warnings are silently suppressed instead of fixed.

title: Module 6 – Microservices with Docker
overview: Built a microservice architecture with Flask, PostgreSQL, and RabbitMQ, connected via publisher/consumer services running in Docker Compose.
learned: I learned how independent services communicate asynchronously through a message queue instead of direct calls.

title: Module 7 – Cloud Deployment on AWS
overview: Deployed the microservice stack to an AWS EC2 instance using Docker Compose, with proper IAM permissions and environment-based secrets.
learned: I learned how much more there is to deploying software in the cloud versus running it locally, from permissions to networking to secrets management.

title: Module 8 – AWS SageMaker Data Analysis
overview: Built a Jupyter notebook pipeline on SageMaker that loads data from S3, cleans and validates it, runs statistical tests, and generates a PDF analytics report.
learned: I learned how easily invalid data can silently corrupt downstream statistics if it isn't validated carefully before analysis.

title: Module 9 – KMeans Clustering
overview: Applied KMeans clustering to admissions data to identify natural groupings by program and applicant profile.
learned: I learned how unsupervised clustering can reveal structure in data without predefined labels, and how sensitive it is to preprocessing choices.

title: Module 10 – Data Dashboard
overview: Built an interactive Dash dashboard analyzing the Kaggle Diamonds dataset with Seaborn and Plotly visualizations.
learned: I learned how to build a full data pipeline from raw cleaning through interactive, browser-based visualization.

title: Module 11 – MLOps with MLflow
overview: Added MLflow experiment tracking to a KMeans clustering pipeline, logging parameters, metrics, and artifacts across runs.
learned: I learned why tracking experiments systematically matters once you're iterating on models, not just running them once.

title: Module 12 – Neural Network from Scratch
overview: Built a two-layer neural network using only NumPy to predict admissions outcomes, without relying on a deep learning framework.
learned: I learned how forward and backward propagation actually work under the hood, instead of treating them as a black box.

title: Module 13 – Fine-Tuning DistilBERT
overview: Fine-tuned a pretrained DistilBERT model on admissions data and deployed it behind a Flask 'Will You Get In?' prediction page.
learned: I learned how to take a pretrained language model, adapt it to a specific task, and deploy it as a real, usable web feature.
